proposal.summary: Collision attack on long (64-bit) PGP key IDs used in Gradle dependency verification metadata allows attackers to exploit short key IDs specified in trusted-key or pgp elements; fixed in Gradle 8.0 and patched in 6.9.4 and 7.6.1. Workaround: use only full fingerprint IDs in trusted-key or pgp elements.
proposal.affected_product: Gradle (versions prior to 8.0; patches available in 6.9.4 and 7.6.1)

AV.quote: Users of dependency verification in Gradle are vulnerable if they use long IDs for PGP keys in a `trusted-key` or `pgp` element in their dependency verification metadata file.

C.quote: This is a collision attack on long IDs (64bits) for PGP keys.

I.quote: This is a collision attack on long IDs (64bits) for PGP keys.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Verify affected Gradle versions in-use; advise users to upgrade to Gradle 8.0 or apply patches (6.9.4, 7.6.1). In the meantime, instruct users to replace any trusted-key or pgp long/short IDs with full fingerprint IDs in dependency verification metadata.

evidence_quotes.claim: Vulnerability affects users of dependency verification when using long IDs
evidence_quotes.quote: Users of dependency verification in Gradle are vulnerable if they use long IDs for PGP keys in a `trusted-key` or `pgp` element in their dependency verification metadata file.

evidence_quotes.claim: Nature of the vulnerability (collision attack on 64-bit IDs)
evidence_quotes.quote: This is a collision attack on long IDs (64bits) for PGP keys.
The problem is fixed in Gradle 8.0 and above.

evidence_quotes.claim: Patches available for older release lines
evidence_quotes.quote: The problem is also patched in Gradle 6.9.4 and 7.6.1.
As a workaround, use only full fingerprint IDs for `trusted-key` or `pgp` element in the metadata is a protection against this issue.
